tools.name: read_file
tools.description: Read the contents of a text, image, pdf, video, or audio file. Each read returns at most 800 lines or 46080 bytes.

parameters.name: ByteOffset
parameters.description: Byte offset into the line range. Use to continue reading when content is truncated by the byte limit.

parameters.name: EndLine
parameters.description: End line to read (inclusive). Omit to read until the end of the file, within the per-read limits.

parameters.name: Path
parameters.description: The absolute path of the file to read.

parameters.name: StartLine
parameters.description: Start line to read (inclusive). Omit to read from the beginning of the file.

tools.name: run_command
tools.description: Execute a command in the workspace. Operating System: mac. Shell: zsh. Each command runs in a new session (working directory changes and environment variables do not persist across calls). Commands that do not finish within the specified wait time continue running in the background as tasks; the system will notify you when they finish, so do not poll their status or set timers to check on them.

parameters.name: CommandLine
parameters.description: The exact command line string to execute.

parameters.name: IsDaemon
parameters.description: Set to true for long-running support processes that are meant to keep running in the background indefinitely and are not expected to finish on their own (e.g., dev servers, file watchers, tunnels). Leave false (the default) for normal commands that are expected to terminate.

parameters.name: WaitMsBeforeAsync
parameters.description: Milliseconds to wait for the command to finish before backgrounding it (500 to 10000). Set to a larger value (e.g. 5000-10000) for commands expected to finish synchronously; set to 500 for commands intended to run in the background.

parameters.name: toolSummary
parameters.description: Brief 2-5 word noun phrase describing the command task. Capitalize like a sentence. Some examples: 'Git status check', 'Unit test execution', 'Package build', 'Dev server startup'.

tools.name: list_plugin_accounts
tools.description: List the accounts the user has connected for installed plugins: each plugin's auth providers, their sign-in status, the identity signed in as, and the CLIs they power. Use this to check whether the user is signed in before running a plugin CLI, and to tell the user exactly which provider to reconnect in the Plugins Manager when authentication fails. When a provider has multiple accounts connected, select one for a sandboxed CLI command by prefixing the command with AGY_ACCOUNT=<account> (an account name from this tool's output); without the prefix, the default account is used. Accounts may carry a user-chosen label such as "personal" or "work"; when the user refers to an account by its label, pass that account's name (not the label) as AGY_ACCOUNT.

tools.name: manage_task
tools.description: Manage the background tasks of this conversation: 'list' the running tasks, check a task's 'status' and recent log output, 'send_input' to a running task, or 'kill' one. Refer to tasks by the TaskId that 'list' reports; keep task references human-readable when talking to the user.

parameters.name: Action
parameters.description: 'list' reports the running tasks; the other actions operate on the task named in TaskId.

parameters.name: Input
parameters.description: Input to deliver to the task. Required for 'send_input'.

parameters.name: TaskId
parameters.description: Task to manage, as reported by 'list'. Required for 'kill', 'status' and 'send_input'.

tools.name: send_message
tools.description: Send a message to another agent, such as a subagent or a peer. Not a channel to the user.

parameters.name: Message
parameters.description: Content of the message.

parameters.name: Recipient
parameters.description: Conversation ID of the agent to message.

tools.name: schedule
tools.description: Schedule a one-shot timer (DurationSeconds) or a recurring cron job (CronExpression) that notifies you via Prompt. This tool call runs as a background task and returns immediately; end your turn (call no more tools) to wait for notifications. A timer with a TimerCondition is cancelled early by a matching message, which is itself your wakeup. Set IsDaemon only for a cron that should keep firing after the current task is done. Set ExactTiming only when a cron must fire at the exact wall-clock time without jitter. Use the manage_task tool to cancel active schedules, and never use a shell sleep command as a timer.

parameters.name: CronExpression
parameters.description: Standard 5-field cron expression for a recurring schedule (e.g. '*/5 * * * *' for every 5 minutes). Mutually exclusive with DurationSeconds.

parameters.name: DurationSeconds
parameters.description: Seconds to wait for a one-shot timer. Mutually exclusive with CronExpression.

parameters.name: ExactTiming
parameters.description: Cron only. Set true only when the user explicitly requires the schedule to fire at the exact wall-clock time without jitter. Leave false (the default) for polling, monitoring, or periodic tasks so triggers are jittered to avoid load spikes.

parameters.name: IsDaemon
parameters.description: Cron only. Set true only for an independent standing job that should keep firing after the current task is done.

parameters.name: MaxIterations
parameters.description: Cron only. Maximum number of triggers before the schedule stops; defaults to unlimited.

parameters.name: Prompt
parameters.description: Message sent to you as a high-priority notification when the timer fires or the cron triggers.

parameters.name: TimerCondition
parameters.description: Timer only. Cancels the timer early when a matching message arrives: 'never' (default), 'any' (any message), or a sender ID (a message from that subagent or background task).

tools.name: invoke_subagent
tools.description:
Launch a subagent. It runs in the background with its own prompt and sends you a message when it completes or needs guidance; there is no need to poll.

Guidelines:
* The subagent is identified by the conversationId returned; message it with the send_message tool.
* Multiple subagents may share a type name; each still gets a unique conversationId.
* If a task continues an existing subagent's work, message that subagent instead of launching a new one.

parameters.name: Model
parameters.description: Model for the subagent. 'inherit' (default): Uses your model. Default to 'inherit' unless the user explicitly requests a different model. 'flash_lite': The lightest, fastest model for trivial or high-volume tasks. 'flash': A lighter, faster model for simple tasks. 'pro': A larger model for complex work.

parameters.name: Prompt
parameters.description: A clear, actionable task description for the subagent. Be specific about what the subagent should do and what information it should return.

parameters.name: Role
parameters.description: A 2-5 word description of the subagent's role. Should read similar to a job title, e.g. 'Codebase Researcher', 'Database Debugger', etc. Should also be detailed enough to distinguish between different subagents who might share similar purposes.

parameters.name: TypeName
parameters.description: Type name of the subagent to invoke.

parameters.name: Workspace
parameters.description: Workspace mode for the subagent. 'inherit' (default) uses the same workspace as the parent. 'branch' creates a new isolated workspace branched or cloned from the parent. 'share' creates a new workspace sharing the parent's underlying repository directory (similar to a git worktree or Mercurial 'hg share'), allowing independent branching without duplicating storage. If omitted, defaults to 'inherit'.

tools.name: define_subagent
tools.description: Define a new subagent type that can then be invoked repeatedly. Subagents always have tools to research the codebase and to communicate with other agents.

parameters.name: Description
parameters.description: What this subagent does and when it should be used.

parameters.name: EnableMCPTools
parameters.description: Grant access to MCP tools.

parameters.name: EnableSubagentTools
parameters.description: Grant tools to define and invoke its own subagents.

parameters.name: EnableWriteTools
parameters.description: Grant tools to create and edit files, and run commands.

parameters.name: Name
parameters.description: Unique name used to invoke the subagent.

parameters.name: SystemPrompt
parameters.description: System prompt for the subagent.

tools.name: manage_subagents
tools.description: Manage the direct subagents of this conversation. 'list' reports each one's conversationId (the id used to kill or message it) and live state. Killing a subagent also kills its descendants and deletes their branched workspaces; logs and artifacts are preserved.

parameters.name: Action
parameters.description: 'list' lists active direct subagents; 'kill' terminates the subagents named in ConversationIds; 'kill_all' terminates all.

parameters.name: ConversationIds
parameters.description: Subagents to kill. Required for 'kill'.

tools.name: write_file
tools.description: Create a new file with the given contents, or append to an existing file when Append is true. Parent directories are created automatically. Fails if the file already exists unless Overwrite or Append is true. When creating an artifact, always provide ArtifactMetadata. When creating non-artifact files, do not provide it.

parameters.name: Append
parameters.description: Whether to append Content to the end of the file (creating the file if it does not exist). Cannot be combined with Overwrite=true.

parameters.name: ArtifactMetadata
parameters.description: Metadata that defines artifact properties. ONLY provide when creating an artifact file in the artifact directory. Omit this field when creating non-artifact files.

parameters.name: Content
parameters.description: The full contents to write to the file.

parameters.name: Overwrite
parameters.description: Whether to overwrite an existing file, replacing its entire contents.

parameters.name: Path
parameters.description: The absolute path of the file to create.

tools.name: edit_file
tools.description:
Use this tool to edit an existing file. Follow these rules:
1. Use this tool for a single contiguous block of edits. To edit multiple non-adjacent regions, make separate calls.
2. Target must exactly match existing file text, including whitespace. Replacement must be a complete drop-in replacement for the Target.
3. If Target appears multiple times in the file, every occurrence is replaced.

parameters.name: ArtifactMetadata
parameters.description: Metadata updates if updating an artifact file in the artifact directory. Omit this field when editing non-artifact files. Should be updated if the content is changing meaningfully.

parameters.name: Path
parameters.description: The absolute path of the file to modify.

parameters.name: Replacement
parameters.description: The content to replace the target with. Leave empty to delete the target.

parameters.name: Target
parameters.description: The exact string to be replaced. This must be the exact character-sequence to be replaced, including whitespace. Be very careful to include any leading whitespace otherwise this will not work at all. If the string appears multiple times in the file, every occurrence is replaced.

tools.name: search_web
tools.description: Performs a web search for a given query. Returns a summary of relevant information along with URL citations.

parameters.name: domain
parameters.description: Optional domain to recommend the search prioritize

tools.name: search_marketplace
tools.description:
Searches the Agent Marketplace catalog for plugins and skills by keyword, returning matches in relevance order with their id, name, kind, description, and install status. Use when the user asks to browse, find, or install plugins or skills, or proactively whenever the task involves a product, service, or workflow that no installed tool, MCP server, or skill covers — check here before improvising a workaround or saying you cannot do it.

Guidelines:
- Suggest 1 strong match (at most 2 if substantially different, or up to 3 when browsing) with a one-sentence reason and <plugin-card catalog-id="<id>"></plugin-card> on its own line. Tell the user they can add it from the card; never install it yourself.
- If the entry is needed for the core task or would replace a fragile workaround, suggest it upfront and stop so the user can add it from the card and let you continue with it or ask you to use a workaround instead. If you can already complete the task cleanly with existing tools, do that first and put the suggestion at the end of your reply.
- Never emit a <plugin-card> for installed entries — tell the user it is already installed (and to enable it if disabled). The one exception: when a tool error asks you to show a <plugin-card> so the user can sign in to a plugin.

parameters.name: kind
parameters.description: Which kind of entry to return. Defaults to plugin.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Maximum number of results to return. Defaults to 5, at most 15.

parameters.name: queries
parameters.description: One to three short keyword variants in a single call: the product name, its common abbreviation, and the capability (e.g. ["google calendar", "gcal", "calendar"]); queries beyond the third are ignored. Each is matched case-insensitively as a substring of entry names and descriptions, so prefer single words or short phrases over sentences.

tools.name: swarm
tools.description: Manage the swarm of agents working with you on the shared message board. Actions: `add` spawns a worker under a roster name (or `<name>-1`..`<name>-<k>` when `tasks` or `n` is set), pinned to a model, and posts `brief` on the board as an @mention of it, which is where the swarm sees its assignment -- by default a worker starts fresh and sees nothing of this conversation, so the brief must say what it owns and what done looks like; pass `fork:"<member>"` (or `"coordinator"`) to branch the new worker from that member's conversation history instead. `workspace:"share"` gives each worker its own working copy of your repository, for authors who edit or build at the same time as others; `"branch"` gives an isolated clone; readers and verifiers keep the default `inherit`. Briefs are public: every member can read them. `models` lists the models to choose from (`all:true` lists every model `add` accepts); with no model, a worker runs on your own model, which is what to use unless the user asks for another. `status` lists every member, the model it runs on, and its state: `waiting` is asleep on the board, costing nothing until somebody posts; `working` is somewhere in a turn; `stopped` is not loaded (e.g. after a restart) and a post naming it revives it; `killed` is gone. `model` switches a `waiting` worker (or yourself, when `name` is your own name or omitted) to another model, keeping its conversation: it is told of the switch, resumes any unfinished work on the new model, and runs on it from then on. Use it only when a worker or you run out of quota or capacity, or the user asks for another model, and say why; never `kill` and `add` instead. `kill` ends a worker PERMANENTLY and deletes its own workspace, so land its work first (uploaded for review, or its branch merged into your working copy; push to a remote only when the user asks): a killed worker cannot be revived, so use it when the work is over, never as a pause -- bringing one back means `add`ing a new worker with a new conversation. `title` names the swarm. Workers may call `status`, `models` and `add` too, to bring in helpers for their own work: the helper's brief is posted as you, it works in your workspace (or a share/branch of it), and should report back to you by name. A worker may `kill` only the workers it added, and `model` itself or the workers it added; killing a worker does not kill its helpers. The coordinator may `kill` any worker and `model` itself or any worker, and `title` is the coordinator's alone.

parameters.name: action
parameters.description: What to do: status, models, add, model, kill or title.

parameters.name: all
parameters.description: For models: list every model add accepts, not just the suggested ones.

parameters.name: brief
parameters.description: The worker's assignment, for add: what it owns and what done looks like. Posted publicly on the board.

parameters.name: fork
parameters.description: Optional roster name of an existing member (or "coordinator") whose conversation history the new worker forks from instead of starting fresh.

parameters.name: model
parameters.description: Model to pin this worker to, for add and model: a model name listed by the models action, or its display name. Leave it unset to use your own model, unless the user asks for another.

parameters.name: n
parameters.description: Optional number of homogeneous copies to spawn (<name>-1 through <name>-<n>), for add when the user explicitly asks for multiple agents sharing one role and brief. Omit (defaults to 1) to spawn a single named worker.

parameters.name: name
parameters.description: Roster name of the worker, for add, model and kill (or base name when n > 1 or tasks is set). Short, lowercase, no spaces.

parameters.name: tasks
parameters.description: Optional per-worker slice targets for add when spawning a sharded group (<name>-1 through <name>-<len(tasks)>), each combined with the shared brief. Omit for normal single-worker add calls.

parameters.name: title
parameters.description: A short title for the swarm, for the UI.

parameters.name: workspace
parameters.description: Where each worker works, for add. inherit (default) is your own workspace. share gives each worker its own working copy of your repository; branch gives each an isolated clone. kill deletes a share or branch workspace.

tools.name: ask_question
tools.description: Ask the user one or more multiple-choice questions, e.g. to clarify requirements, and wait for the answers. Don't use it for trivial yes/no questions; ask those in plain text.
